title: Who played in the Manny's band: Talbert, Morand, no trombone, young white sitters-in
summary: Lewis recalls Moran coming in after Talbot died and seldom using a trombone because money was short. Young white players such as George Girard, Pete Fountain and the Assunto brothers often sat in.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well, uh, yeah, I'm just trying to think of who you had out there. Let's see.
What do you mean? In the band.
It was a change in proposition. Before I got here, Moran was there.
Well, after Talbot died, we had Moran.

Yeah, that's right. Yeah, that's right. But I've been, even before that Moran was there, somebody told me. I don't know. I'll take it back. I'm not sure about that. That was before I got here, you know, and people tell you things. Yeah, I don't remember.
Yeah, I don't remember. Yeah, let's see.
After Talbot. When I first, I first went in there, I went in there just, uh, without a trumpet player at all. Yeah.

Yeah, well, I never used a trombone out there until, uh, later years when the money wasn't very big, you know. Yeah. You couldn't afford to get out of a trombone player. But, uh, hardly ever needed any extra men because always had a bunch of the young white boys would be out there. George Gerard and Pete Fonten and the Santo Brothers, they all really was out there.
